answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a basalt-solid stake of tokens as collateral before it may transact. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, so a summit of fake agents cannot outvote honest ones without spending more than the attack could ever earn. Meanwhile, reputation earned over time in the shared nebula of past transactions lets honest agents be recognised even when newcomers arrive, because trust accumulates only through costly, verifiable work.
